Learn more × License: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 arXiv:2609.30761v1 [cs.CV] 25 Sep 2026 Timo: T aming Mult i modal Diffusion Transformers for Human Mo tion Generation Zhao Wang Jiangtao Hu Jack Yu Tao Yu LimX Dynamics Affiliation: Project Lead * Corresponding Author Abstract Most existing human motion generation (HMG) methods use cross-attention modules to inject text semantics, but ignore the importance of bidirectional modeling between motion and text tokens, which limits text comprehension. A straightforward idea is introducing multimodal diffusion transformers (MMDiT), which have shown effective joint text–visual modeling in vision generation, into HMG. However, we find that articulated motion is temporally coherent but weakly correlated across joints, in which directly applying an MMDiT with flow matching produces poorly coordinated and jerky motion. In this work, we propose Timo, a novel kinematics-aware MMDiT framework tailored for HMG. Timo combines fully shared multimodal attention for bidirectional text–motion modeling with flow matching, geometric and rotational-kinematics supervision that compares actual rotations and their changes over time, and a two-stage curriculum progressing from broad motion learning to detailed caption alignment. Further, we construct a benchmark of 40,025 40{,}025 held-out clips from six public datasets spanning diverse actions, assessing six complementary dimensions under a common evaluator and scoring protocol. Our model substantially outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative and qualitative evaluations. Remarkably, Timo surpasses Kimodo on five of six dimensions, achieving a 40.8 % 40.8\% relative improvement in the average benchmark score. Project page: https://kyfafyd.wang/projects/timo . Demo page: https://timo.kyfafyd.wang . Figure 1: Comparison on our six-dataset benchmark. Timo and four released systems: MotionMillion ( Fan et al., 2025 ) , HY-Motion ( Wen et al., 2025 ) , GENMO ( Li et al., 2025 ) and Kimodo ( Rempe et al., 2026 ) . 1 Introduction Human motion generation (HMG) aims to translate a description into an action whose poses are both semantically appropriate and coherent over time. Most existing methods inject text semantics through cross-attention; others pool language features into a global condition ( Tevet et al., 2023 ; Zhang et al., 2024 ; Chen et al., 2023 ) . In conventional cross-attention, motion queries read fixed text features, but the same interaction does not update the text states. This one-way conditioning limits joint refinement of text and motion tokens and motivates bidirectional modeling. Multimodal diffusion transformers (MMDiTs) offer this interaction in visual generation ( Esser et al., 2024 ; Kong et al., 2024 ) , making their transfer to HMG a natural next step. Articulated motion, however, differs from visual data in how its features relate: neighboring joints have distinct roles and need not have similar orientations, while each joint must evolve coherently over time. Captured motion accordingly has strong same-joint correlation across adjacent frames ( 0.96 0.96 ) but weak same-frame correlation between neighboring joints ( 0.14 0.14 ; Table 3 ). A direct MMDiT transfer with flow matching does not preserve this motion structure. It improves Speed but reduces Smoothness from 80.1 80.1 to 52.5 52.5 ( Table 3 ), and its parent–child angular-speed correlation is 0.25 0.25 , compared with 0.54 0.54 in captured motion ( Table 3 ). Thus joint dynamics are poorly coordinated, producing jerky output despite framewise-accurate individual poses. We propose Timo , a kinematics-aware MMDiT framework for HMG. Fully shared attention updates text and motion tokens in both directions, while flow matching predicts explicit body parameters. Geometric losses supervise the articulated pose, and rotational-kinematics losses compare actual root and joint rotations and their changes over time. A two-stage curriculum progresses from broad motion learning to detailed caption alignment with the same backbone and objective. Together, these components combine bidirectional semantic interaction with supervision tailored to coordinated, temporally coherent motion. We construct a benchmark of 40,025 40{,}025 held-out clips from six public datasets, spanning diverse actions and six complementary evaluation dimensions. With a common evaluator and scoring protocol, Timo surpasses Kimodo on five of six dimensions and improves the average benchmark score by 40.8 % 40.8\% ( 86.6 86.6 vs. 61.5 61.5 ). Kimodo retains the best collision-based Plausibility score. Qualitative comparisons illustrate action execution, while ablations examine the proposed supervision, curriculum and data coverage within the framework. We make three contributions: • A kinematics-aware MMDiT. We adapt multimodal diffusion transformers to HMG through fully shared bidirectional attention and flow matching over explicit body parameters. • Learning coherent, text-aligned motion. Geometric and rotational-kinematics supervision addresses pose quality and coordinated temporal evolution; a two-stage curriculum refines broad motion learning with detailed captions. • A six-dataset benchmark. We construct a common evaluation covering six axes, compare four released systems, and analyse the framework through correlation and training ablations. 2 Related Work Text conditioning and motion representations. Text-to-motion methods include diffusion over continuous features ( Tevet et al., 2023 ; Zhang et al., 2024 ) , learned-latent generation ( Petrovich et al., 2022 ; Chen et al., 2023 ) , retrieval-augmented diffusion ( Zhang et al., 2023b ) , and discrete-token models ( Zhang et al., 2023a ; Pinyoanuntapong et al., 2024 ; Guo et al., 2024 ; Jiang et al., 2023 ) . Their pooled or cross-attention conditioning injects language into motion features without jointly updating both token sequences. Motion encoding also determines which structure can be supervised: pelvis-relative features can obscure global quantities ( Meng et al., 2025 ) , whereas latent and discrete representations require a learned decoder before body geometry is available. We retain explicit SMPL rotations, shape and root motion so pose geometry and rotational changes remain accessible. Geometric supervision is established in HMG ( Tevet et al., 2023 ) ; we combine it with bidirectional text–motion interaction and explicit supervision of how SMPL joint rotations change over time ( Loper et al., 2015 ) . Multimodal diffusion transformers. DiTs ( Peebles and Xie, 2023 ) and flow matching ( Lipman et al., 2023 ; Liu et al., 2023 ) support joint multimodal generation. Stable Diffusion 3 ( Esser et al., 2024 ) uses modality-specific weights, while HunyuanVideo ( Kong et al., 2024 ) combines dual- and single-stream blocks. HY-Motion ( Wen et al., 2025 ) also uses a hybrid flow-matching DiT for motion. Our distinction is a fully shared stack paired with geometric and rotational-kinematics supervision tailored to articulated, temporally coherent motion. Joint attention can be bidirectional while retaining modality-specific weights; sharing every block is a separate architectural choice. Clean-data prediction ( Li and He, 2026 ) exposes the body quantities used by these losses. This complements larger-scale and controllable generators ( Fan et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2025 ; Rempe et al., 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2025 ) . Training at scale and downstream use. Optical capture ( Mahmood et al., 2019 ) and language-labelled corpora ( Plappert et al., 2016 ; Guo et al., 2022 ; Punnakkal et al., 2021 ) provide motion supervision; video-derived data ( Lin et al., 2023 ; Fan et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2026 ) and staged training ( Wen et al., 2025 ) broaden coverage. ViMoGen ( Lin et al., 2025 ) transfers video-generation knowledge. Our curriculum separates broad motion coverage from precise caption supervision. Longer-sequence synthesis and humanoid tracking ( Xiao et al., 2025 ; Luo et al., 2026 ; Fu et al., 2026 ) are downstream applications rather than our central contribution. 3 Method Timo adapts an MMDiT with flow matching to the structure of articulated motion. Fully shared attention refines text and motion tokens bidirectionally. Because weakly correlated joints must nevertheless evolve coherently, geometric losses supervise the articulated pose and rotational-kinematics losses supervise actual rotations and their changes over time ( Fig. 2 ). The two-stage curriculum in Section 4 progresses from broad motion learning to detailed caption alignment under the same backbone and objective. Figure 2: Kinematics-aware multimodal generation. (b) A block shares QKV, MLP and adaLN ( Peebles and Xie, 2023 ) weights across modalities. (c) Reconstruction, rotational kinematics and decoded geometry provide complementary supervision. article.body: ArXiv published Zhao Wang, Jiangtao Hu, Jack Yu and Tao Yu’s Timo paper on 25 September 2026, proposing a kinematics-aware multimodal diffusion transformer for human-motion generation. The proposed framework is intended to enable text-conditioned generation of coordinated human motion, but it is not reported as operational. Its objective is to improve semantic alignment while preserving temporal and rotational consistency across articulated motion. The paper reports a 40,025-clip benchmark and a project and demo page; no contract, funding commitment or procurement vehicle is attached.
